topics.title: Bonding in carbon: the covalent bond

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why carbon forms covalent bonds by sharing electrons rather than forming C4+ or C4- ions.
Identify single, double and triple covalent bonds from electron dot structures of simple molecules.
Relate the low melting points, boiling points and poor conductivity of covalent compounds to their bonding.

topics.title: Versatile nature of carbon: catenation, tetravalency and saturation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how catenation and tetravalency allow carbon to form a very large number of stable compounds.
Distinguish saturated from unsaturated carbon compounds using their bonds and structures.
Recognise structural isomers as compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures.
Classify hydrocarbons as alkanes, alkenes or alkynes and as open-chain or cyclic compounds.

topics.title: Functional groups, homologous series and nomenclature

concepts.learning_objective: Identify heteroatoms and functional groups and explain how they decide the properties of a compound.
Describe a homologous series and the gradation of physical properties along it.
Name simple carbon compounds using the correct prefix or suffix for the functional group.
Explain complete and incomplete combustion and the nature of the flames they produce.
Explain the oxidation of alcohols to carboxylic acids by oxidising agents.
Distinguish addition reactions of unsaturated hydrocarbons from substitution reactions of saturated ones.
Describe the properties and reactions of ethanol with sodium and with hot concentrated sulphuric acid.
Describe the properties of ethanoic acid and its reactions with bases, carbonates and hydrogencarbonates.
Explain the formation of esters and their conversion back by saponification.
Explain how soap molecules form micelles that remove oily dirt.
Explain why soap forms scum in hard water and why detergents remain effective in it.
